Predicted Local Distance Difference Test (pLDDT)

pLDDT is AlphaFold's per-residue confidence score (0-100) for the local accuracy of the predicted structure around each residue. Higher values mean AlphaFold expects that residue's local geometry (backbone/nearby atoms) is more reliable.

How to read it
  • pLDDT is typically shown as a line plot along the sequence and/or mapped onto the 3D model as a color gradient.
  • It reflects local confidence, not whether two distant parts of the protein are correctly positioned relative to each other (that's what PAE is for).
Interpretation guide (rule of thumb)
  • >= 90: very high confidence (often near experimental-quality locally)
  • 70-90: generally reliable local structure
  • 50-70: low confidence; interpret with caution
  • < 50: very low confidence; frequently flexible/disordered, or poorly determined

B-factor (Temperature Factor)

In X-ray crystallography, the B-factor reports how “spread out” an atom's electron density is around its average position—often interpreted as a mix of atomic mobility, static disorder (multiple conformations), and model/measurement uncertainty. It's reported in Å².

How to read it
  • Lower B: sharper, better-defined density → atom is more precisely located (or more ordered).
  • Higher B: smeared/weaker density → atom is less precisely located and/or more heterogeneous (flexible, disordered, multiple states).
  • Compare B-factors within the same structure more confidently than across different structures, because refinement strategy and resolution strongly affect scale.

B-factor (Temperature Factor) in cryo-EM-derived PDBs

In models built from EM reconstructions, the B-factor field is still the atomic displacement parameter (ADP) reported in Å², but it often functions as a model-side proxy for how well each atom is supported by the EM density. Depending on the refinement workflow, it can reflect a mix of local positional uncertainty/disorder and how refinement explains imperfect map-model agreement. In some deposits it may be a pseudo-B (assigned or rescaled rather than physically refined).

How to read it
  • Lower B: crisper, better-supported density / more confident placement - atom is more precisely located (or more ordered).
  • Higher B: weaker/broader density / less confident placement - atom is less precisely located and/or more heterogeneous (flexible, multiple states, local disorder).
  • Interpretation depends on refinement: real-space refinement can refine/use B to fit local map features, but some pipelines assign near-constant or heuristic values (pseudo-B).
  • Not the same as map sharpening: per-atom B-factors in the coordinate file are distinct from any global/local B used to sharpen/blur the map volume.
  • Compare within a structure more confidently than across structures, because B-factor scale can vary a lot with map processing, refinement strategy, and resolution.
